original_test_intent: Verify the complete sensor set for the hardware domain called NM, including the source-filtered TEMP_IBC_NM records, and reconcile each specified name, description and reading across IB SDR/Sensor List, OOB SDR/Sensor List and BMC Web.
original_method: First define what physical assembly or network module NM denotes and whether TEMP_IBC_NM is its complete sensor namespace. Bind every installed NM instance to stable records, retain complete IB/OOB inventories at aligned times, capture Web rows and compare typed values, thresholds and state to the approved specification with passive module/link/thermal context.
manual_activity: The platform owner defines NM, maps TEMP_IBC_NM and resolves criteria 3–17; an operator confirms physical instances and complete Web rows, then the owner decides the result.
required_inputs: Authoritative expansion/function/location of NM and each installed instance
Decision whether TEMP_IBC_NM is the complete, partial or incorrect namespace
NM sensor specification and per-instance physical-to-IB/OOB/Web mapping
Sensor types, units, expected ranges/states, thresholds and freshness
Secure access, full Web capture and timestamp/cache/rounding rules
Criteria 3–17 disposition, passive health context and escalation owner
safety_requirements: Do not infer the meaning of NM or silently equate it with the grep string
Keep collection read-only and protect credentials
Retain full inventories before filtering and enumerate every approved NM instance
Do not query the test title as a sensor, truncate results or clear logs
Do not alter module/link state, thresholds or BMC configuration
Stop on identity ambiguity, missing/duplicate/stale reading, channel disagreement, link alarm or thermal excursion
agent_execution_scope: Verify unique source identity and collect complete read-only IB/OOB data
After owner mapping, correlate each NM instance and TEMP_IBC_NM record to Web evidence
Normalize fields and correlate passive link/module/thermal status
Report missing, extra, duplicate, stale and mismatched entries
Perform no naming decision, control action, criteria invention or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Define NM and approve TEMP_IBC_NM scope, population, sensor semantics and mappings
Resolve the criteria-number gap and any omitted NM checks
Review all mapped members and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.status: PACKAGE-GATED NM IDENTITY AND SENSOR RECONCILIATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a versioned definition of NM and its physical instances, bind TEMP_IBC_NM and any companion records, then compare complete IB/OOB/Web evidence with passive health context.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the undefined acronym/scope explicit and prevents a filter string from becoming an unverified hardware model.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item says NM while the procedure filters TEMP_IBC_NM without defining equivalence, and criteria jump from 2 to 18. DeepSeek adds an invented title sensor and incomplete evidence. These ambiguities require owner resolution.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A passive reconciliation path exists once NM identity, mapping and criteria are supplied; these are pending project inputs rather than an intrinsic technical block.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2016 Wistron-BMC-01036-V002: define what physical hardware `NM` denotes and whether `TEMP_IBC_NM` is its complete sensor scope; also confirm whether Criteria 1, 2, 18 is only misnumbered or Criteria 3–17 are missing, and provide the full per-instance IB/OOB/Web acceptance map.

review_improvement: Prevents an undefined acronym and filter from being treated as a complete sensor model, while preserving all source views and explicitly tracking the criteria gap.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source exposes two identities—NM and TEMP_IBC_NM—but gives no proof they are coextensive. TEMP suggests a temperature channel, while NM could own additional status, power or link sensors or multiple physical instances. Thus completeness cannot be judged from that filter alone. Full inventories may be collected safely, but the owner must define the hardware boundary and the unexplained criteria 3–17 before acceptance.
